sources.title: B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10 (author-published undergraduate textbook, 246 PDF pages); signature (+---) converted to (-+++) and c=1 formulas converted to x^0 = ct
sources.locator: Section 1.4 'The Lorentz transformation' pp. 30-32 (equation (1), the light-line/determinant and interval-invariance checks, Examples 11-14), Sections 2.3 'Additional postulates' and 2.4 'Other axiomatizations' pp. 46-49 (P3-P6, E1-E2, T1-T2 and the comparison), and Section 8.3 'Boosts and rotations' pp. 174-176 (8.3.1 rotations, 8.3.2 boosts, 8.3.3 Thomas precession)

contents.name: Section 1.4, equation (1): t' = gamma t - v gamma x, x' = -v gamma t + gamma x, the 1+1 Lorentz transformation with c=1 and the figure explaining its stretching/squishing of the diagonals
contents.support: The definition fixes the same passive sign convention, generalizes it to a parameter beta in R^3, and converts the source's c=1, (+---) presentation to x^0 = ct with eta = diag(-1,1,1,1); the conversion is an explicit adaptation, not a new claim.

contents.name: Section 1.4: verification of equation (1) by (1) preservation of the speed-of-light lines x = +-t and (2) determinant equal to 1, and the alternative check of invariance of the spacetime interval
contents.support: The light-line and determinant checks are the 1+1 instance of the general boost verification; the local lemma proves metric preservation, determinant one and cone preservation for every beta from the parallel/perpendicular decomposition.

contents.name: Examples 11-13: observers agree on their relative speeds (Lorentz transformations with velocities v and -v are inverses), motion in the opposite direction, and the other quadrants of the transformation
contents.support: The worked example verifies that the inverse boost has the opposite parameter and computes the direction of relative motion of the two chart origins.

contents.name: Example 14: numerical invariance at v = 3/5, with events (t,x) = (0,0), (13,11) mapping to (0,0), (8,4) and interval 13^2 - 11^2 = 8^2 - 4^2 = 48 in the (+---) convention
contents.support: The worked example reproduces the mapping exactly and records the interval -48 in the eta_0 = diag(-1,1) convention used by this library.

contents.name: Section 1.4 remark: the Lorentz transformation is not reducible to length contraction and time dilation, and 1+1 dimensions are used only for convenience
contents.reason: This is a caution against an erroneous reduction; the library represents the transformation by its exact algebraic statements and worked examples, and no separate formal claim exists to scaffold.

contents.name: Sections 2.3-2.4: the symmetry postulates P3 (homogeneity and isotropy), P4 (existence of inertial frames), P5 (equivalence of uniformly moving frames), P6 (relativity of time), and Einstein's E1-E2 together with the T1-T2 maximal-proper-time system
contents.support: The remark records which formal assumptions those verbal systems contain and lists the reconstruction obligations (homogeneity/isotropy, inertial-frame existence, operational simultaneity, affine group preserving a quadratic form, global topology) that this framework does not discharge.

contents.name: Section 2.4.3: the claim that the P, E and T axiomatizations are logically equivalent, and the comparison with doubly-special relativity
contents.reason: The claimed equivalence of the verbal axiom systems is neither re-proved nor used here; the remark treats reconstruction from them as an open obligation, so there is no scaffolded claim to attach this source-level assertion to.

contents.name: Section 2.2.3: the flatness postulate P2, the Gravity Probe B precession narrative and the small-region qualification of flatness
contents.reason: Flatness of the adopted model is a primitive assumption of this framework, and curvature tests belong to the general-relativity content; no special-relativity item is derived from this narrative here.

contents.name: Section 2.5: proof that spacetime area in the x-t plane is invariant from the postulates P1-P6 via the lattice construction
contents.reason: The area argument is a reconstruction device internal to the source's own axiomatization; this framework adopts the affine interval structure and proves determinant-one and interval invariance directly, so the argument is not part of the scaffold.

contents.name: Section 8.3.2 'Boosts': the numerical example in which a boost along x followed by a boost along y differs from the reversed order, with the discrepancy a rotation of order v^2
contents.support: The counterexample replaces the source's rounded decimals by exact rational matrices at beta = 3/5 and exhibits differing entries of the two products.

contents.name: Section 8.3.1 'Rotations': rotations about different axes do not commute, with the numerical discrepancy of order theta^2
contents.reason: Noncommutativity of spatial rotations is ordinary three-dimensional rotation-group structure already available through the imported orthogonal-operator material; no special-relativity-specific claim needs scaffolding.

contents.name: Section 8.3.3 'Thomas precession': the gyroscope-around-a-square example and the low-velocity precession formula Omega = a x v, together with its atomic-physics application
contents.reason: A physical precession rate requires an accelerated-observer spin model with additional structure; this page supplies only the algebraic Thomas-Wigner rotation of an explicit boost composition in ex-sr-boost-rotation-factorization-worked.

sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Chapter 1 'Special relativity and flat spacetime' pp. 3-7 (PDF pp. 10-14)
sources.locator: Chapter 1 pp. 3-7 (PDF pp. 10-14): equations (1.3)-(1.21), the paragraphs following (1.14) on the Lorentz group, and the light-cone discussion on p. 7

contents.name: Equations (1.3)-(1.9): the interval s^2 = -(c dt)^2 + (dx)^2 + (dy)^2 + (dz)^2, inertial frames, c as a fixed conversion factor, and the metric eta_{mu nu} with s^2 = eta_{mu nu} dx^mu dx^nu
contents.reason: The interval, the metric component matrix and the conversion constant c are supplied on the earlier spacetime-primitives page (scaffolded as batch 1 of this run); this page consumes them and does not re-derive them.

contents.name: Equations (1.10)-(1.15): translations, x' = Lambda x, the condition eta = Lambda^T eta Lambda defining Lorentz transformations, and the name O(3,1) for the Lorentz group
contents.support: The definition states the same metric-preservation condition on the abstract Lorentz vector space and records the matrix criterion M^T eta_0 M = eta_0 in an eta-orthonormal basis, with the group structure proved in a separate lemma.

contents.name: Equations (1.17)-(1.18): the rotation example (1.17) and the boost matrix (1.18) with rapidity parameter phi
contents.support: The boost definition is the same matrix in the passive convention, stated with the dimensionless parameter beta and an arbitrary spatial direction; the rotation matrix of (1.17) is the model for def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame.

contents.name: Equations (1.19)-(1.21): t' = t cosh phi - x sinh phi, x' = -t sinh phi + x cosh phi, the velocity v = tanh phi, and the conversion to t' = gamma(t - vx), x' = gamma(x - vt)
contents.support: The lemma proves beta = tanh r, gamma = cosh r and the displayed hyperbolic matrix from the exponential definitions, and derives the composition law from the addition formula.

contents.name: Paragraphs after (1.14): rotations, boosts and discrete time/space reversals; the proper Lorentz group SO(3,1) as the exclusion of the reversals; non-commutativity of the general six-parameter group; and the Poincare group of translations and Lorentz transformations
contents.support: The counterexample supplies the exact matrices Pi and T, their determinants and their orthochrony classes, witnessing that excluding the discrete transformations is a genuine restriction and that det = 1 alone is not enough.

contents.name: Paragraph after (1.14), continued: the Poincare group as the ten-parameter group of translations and Lorentz transformations
contents.support: The affine Lorentz maps of the definition are exactly the compositions of a translation with a linear Lorentz map, which is the source's Poincare group without its spinorial generalisation.

contents.name: Light-cone discussion (p. 7): the set of light-speed trajectories x = +-t is invariant under Lorentz transformations, light cones are naturally divided into future and past, and timelike/spacelike/null separation
contents.support: Clause (ii) of the physics theorem records the chart-independence of the causal classification and of the future/past orientation, as the coordinate form of cone preservation by proper orthochronous Lorentz maps.

contents.name: Spacetime diagram paragraph: under a boost the x'-axis is t = x tanh phi and the t'-axis is t = x/tanh phi, and the axes scissor together instead of remaining Euclidean-orthogonal
contents.reason: The diagrammatic axis description is a visualization of the boost formula that is already scaffolded as an exact algebraic statement; it carries no separate formal claim for the library.

contents.name: Closing paragraph of the SR section: applying the boost formulae leads to time dilation, length contraction, and the general six-parameter matrix is not written down explicitly
contents.reason: The measurement consequences of the boost (time dilation, length contraction) presuppose simultaneity and radar protocols and are proved on the observer-measurements page; the omission of the general six-parameter matrix is a source gap, not a result to harvest.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Mathematical Tripos Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), Section 2.2 'Lorentzian signature' pp. 26-28 (PDF pp. 27-29); Internet Archive copy of the original https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/hsr1000/part3_gr_lectures.pdf
sources.locator: Section 2.1 p. 25 (inverse metric and index manipulation) and Section 2.2 'Lorentzian signature' pp. 26-28 (PDF pp. 27-29), equations (2.9)-(2.12), the exercise on orthogonality, and the causal-classification definitions

contents.name: Section 2.2 p. 27, equations (2.9)-(2.10): orthonormal bases at a point and eta_{mu nu} A^mu_rho A^nu_sigma = eta_{rho sigma} as the defining equations of a Lorentz transformation
contents.support: The definition states exactly this matrix criterion, adapted from a point of a Lorentzian manifold to the abstract Lorentz vector space of the affine model, and proves its basis-independence.

contents.name: Section 2.2 p. 27: timelike/null/spacelike and causal vectors, and the double light cone separating timelike from spacelike vectors, with causal vectors falling into two disconnected sets
contents.reason: The causal classification, the two components of the timelike set and the closed cones are defined and proved on the earlier spacetime-primitives page; this page consumes them in the cone-preservation lemmas.

contents.name: Section 2.2 p. 27, exercise (Examples sheet 1): a nonzero vector orthogonal to a timelike vector is spacelike; orthogonal to a null vector it is spacelike or null; orthogonal to a spacelike vector it may be spacelike, timelike or null
contents.support: The factorization proof uses the timelike case for e_0: the orthogonal complement of the unit timelike vector e_0 is positive definite, immediate in an eta-orthonormal basis and used to identify the restriction B(beta)L|_S as an orthogonal map of a Euclidean three-space.

contents.name: Section 2.2 p. 27, remark: on a Lorentzian manifold tensor components with respect to different orthonormal bases are related exactly as in special relativity
contents.support: The theorem proves the vector, covector, general (r,s), derivative and (2,0)-divergence component laws in the affine model, which is the statement the remark points to.

contents.name: Section 2.1 p. 25 and Section 2.2 p. 26: the inverse metric g^{ab}, the natural isomorphism between vectors and covectors, and lowering/raising of indices on a general tensor
contents.support: The theorem includes the invariance of the metric components eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab} under inertial transitions, which is what makes eta-based raising and lowering commute with the component law.

contents.name: Section 2.2 p. 26: the definition of a Riemannian/Lorentzian manifold as a pair (M,g) with a smooth nondegenerate metric tensor field
contents.reason: The manifold formulation of Lorentzian geometry belongs to the general-relativity framework; this page works with the global affine charts of the flat model and does not import curvature or manifold language.

contents.name: Section 2.2 pp. 27-28: proper time d tau^2 = -g_{mu nu} dx^mu dx^nu along a timelike curve, and the definitions of timelike, null, spacelike and causal curves
contents.reason: Curve regularity, proper time and the four-velocity are the subject of the worldlines-and-clocks page (order 213), which follows this page; the present page proves only the transformation structure those definitions will use.

sources.note: The original DAMTP URL fails full-text fetch in this environment with an SSL certificate verification error (initial attempt plus retries recorded in the batch notes); the cited archive snapshot serves the byte-identical 125-page course (sha256_16 fe8a24c67e884ff1), so the reader-facing URL is the archived copy and the original is retained here as provenance.
